Experiments on a humanoid robot and in the real world show the same failure patterns. We hope PhyDEX will drive the development of physically grounded robot policies.

papers.title: GEOHunter: Mapping a Generative Engine Optimization Network in the Wild
papers.summary: Generative engines synthesize retrieved web pages into answers, recommendations, and rankings. Generative engine optimization (GEO) services sell visibility in these answers by publishing promotional articles on user-generated-content (UGC) platforms for paying clients. Such promotion raises concerns in medical and financial domains, where misleading advice can cause harm. To study the severity of this problem, we measure one such paid-content operation across three major Chinese UGC platforms, uncovering 1,985 accounts associated with the network comprising 466,357 inferred promotional placements. We find that the network promotes products across diverse categories through a growing pool of accounts, conducting coordinated campaigns spanning months across multiple platforms while evolving its listicle content over time. Across nine generative engines from both the US and China, we find that 4.5% to 20% of retrievable cited pages are attributable to the network, depending on how strictly attribution is drawn. On eight of these engines, its clients are named in 52% of answers, against 68% for category leaders. Our work demonstrates the effectiveness of UGC GEO placement at influencing generative engine outcomes, and reveals content-level defenses as insufficient against coordinated UGC placements, where account-level and platform-level signals are necessary for proper defense.

papers.title: Multi-institutional grading of Barrett's esophagus dysplasia without stain normalization using a pathology foundation model and multiple instance learning
papers.summary: Barrett's esophagus dysplasia grading suffers substantial inter-observer variability, particularly for low-grade dysplasia, complicating clinical decision-making. We conducted a retrospective multi-institutional diagnostic accuracy study of a foundation model-based deep learning system for dysplasia grading, using 969 H\&E-stained whole slide images from four institutions. Patch-level classifiers trained on expert annotations identified diagnostically relevant regions, followed by attribute-aware multiple instance learning for slide-level classification as non-dysplastic Barrett's esophagus (NDBE), low-grade dysplasia, or high-grade dysplasia. On a held-out test set (n = 130), macro-averaged AUC was 0.96 (95\% CI 0.93--0.98). For binary dysplasia detection, sensitivity was 98\% (80/82) and specificity 81\% (39/48), with a negative likelihood ratio of 0.030 and quadratic-weighted \kap{} of 0.83 against expert consensus. No high-grade dysplasia case was misclassified as NDBE. Performance was consistent across institutions without stain normalization, indicating that stain-robust foundation-model representations may remove the site-specific preprocessing that has constrained prior systems to institution-specific deployment.

papers.title: Susceptibility source separation via Closed-form Alternating Newton-type Optimization
papers.summary: Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping (QSM) provides a bulk magnetic susceptibility estimate per voxel, so contributions from paramagnetic and diamagnetic sources within the same voxel partially cancel. Susceptibility source separation methods identify these compartments by fitting a three-pool complex exponential model to multi-echo gradient-echo (GRE) data. However, conventional voxel-wise fitting with general-purpose constrained solvers requires several hours per whole-brain volume and often fails in high-susceptibility regions. We present CANON-QSM (Closed-form Alternating Newton-type Optimization for QSM), a solver that reformulates the subproblems of the three-pool model and solves them alternately via exact closed-form updates and Newton-type steps, yielding a substantial per-voxel computational speedup. Both in silico and in vivo evaluations demonstrate not only a massive reduction in reconstruction time, completing a whole-brain volume in under two minutes, but also improved accuracy and robustness against artifacts in high-susceptibility regions. Finally, an echo-time analysis of the three-pool model shows that source separation is driven by second-order nonlinearities in signal decay and phase evolution rather than first-order bulk estimates.

papers.title: Superluminal propagation in the magnetic NED reconstruction of the extremal Dymnikova black hole
papers.summary: We reconstruct the magnetic nonlinear electrodynamics (NED) source of the Dymnikova geometry on the branch \(\Iinv>0\) and analyze its electromagnetic perturbations on the fixed background. The reconstruction does not admit a Maxwell limit. The extraordinary characteristic cone gives a transverse speed \(v_\perp^2=(3u-5)/2\), with \(u=r^3/P^3\), which becomes superluminal for \(r>r_{\rm lum}=(7/3)^{1/3}P\). The principal system is pointwise hyperbolic in the finite exterior \(r\ge r_e\), with positive local quadratic energy, but not uniformly hyperbolic up to spatial infinity. The radial effective potential admits an exact reduction, \(V_{\rm em}=f\ell(\ell+1)\mathcal{A}/r^2+ff_{,r}q +f^2(q_{,r}+\frac34q^2)\), behaves as \(V_0\proptoε^2\) near the horizon, and grows as \(27r^4/(4P^6)\) at infinity. It is numerically positive on a fine grid up to \(r=50P\). The Dymnikova reconstruction does not satisfy the hypotheses of the Tomizawa--Suzuki theorem, since it lacks a Maxwell limit, yet it still produces superluminal extraordinary photons. The reconstructed NED branch is therefore mathematically consistent as a source of the Dymnikova background, but not causally acceptable with respect to the physical metric in the asymptotic region. The global positivity of the effective potential and the quasinormal spectrum are left as open problems.

papers.title: Learning Control-Relevant Koopman Representations from Input-Output Trajectories
papers.summary: Predictive accuracy alone does not ensure that data-driven Koopman representations are suitable for output-feedback control. This paper develops a continuous-time framework for learning control-relevant Koopman representations using only measured input-output trajectories. A causal encoder constructs the lifted state from a finite input-output window, and an additive lifted model is identified by integral regression. We distinguish observability, input-map compatibility, controllability, and data informativity. We characterize compatibility with a constant lifted input matrix, quantify input-map mismatch, and, under exact lifting assumptions, relate iterated Lie brackets to the controllable subspace of the lifted realization. A covariance-normalized finite-horizon observability criterion is optimized subject to separate bounds on output-prediction and temporal-consistency errors. Under the stated exactness and observability assumptions, the encoded lifted state depends only on the current nonlinear state. For approximate representations, we bound the difference between encodings of distinct past trajectories ending at the same state. An exactly liftable controlled system provides analytical ground truth, while a controlled Duffing oscillator illustrates the approximate setting, for which an informative exact additive lifting on an open set is shown to be impossible. On the exact benchmark, encoder initialization determines whether the learned representation recovers the analytical lift. In the reported Duffing experiments, observability promotion improves nominal Gramian measures without improving observer-based estimation or tracking, while updating the lifted-state estimate through the encoder at every sampling instant has a larger effect on tracking accuracy.

papers.title: u3lib: An AI-Ready Computational Framework for U(3) Symmetry Algebra, Wigner Coupling, and Racah Recoupling Coefficients
papers.summary: u3lib is a C++ library for U(3)/SU(3) representation-theory calculations in nuclear structure and related applications. It evaluates Wigner coupling and Racah recoupling coefficients using the procedure proposed in 2024 by Dang et al., which avoids the binomial coefficients and alternating sums used in earlier formulations. The library also provides irreducible representations (irreps), dimensions, Casimir invariants, conjugation, and tensor-product decompositions with outer multiplicities. It supports the canonical Gelfand-Tsetlin basis and the physical SU(3) $\supset$ SO(3) basis, including inner multiplicities and the transformation between the two bases. Generator routines return matrix elements in the canonical basis and reduced matrix elements in the physical basis. Python bindings mirror the C++ API. Domain skills supplied with the repository allow an AI assistant with code-execution access to call these routines from natural-language requests.
papers.comment: 15 pages, 1 figure, 3 tables. Code available at https://github.com/Deep-SANE/u3lib

papers.title: MM-SystemOneBias: Evaluating Bias in Multimodal Jev-Style System One Decision Models
papers.summary: When multimodal decision models determine actions, moderation outcomes, or quality judgments, their reliability depends on preserving semantic decisions across presentation changes, ignoring irrelevant additions, and distinguishing information consistent with task evidence from information that conflicts with it. Existing evaluations study decision-interface biases and multimodal model behavior in separate settings, leaving no common protocol to compare multimodal decision models with their backbones on practical tasks. We introduce \textbf{MM-SystemOneBias}, which evaluates 13 models on 5,323 original instances from nine public datasets and 11 task scenarios using six paired interventions: option order, option label, external judgment, image--text description, irrelevant information, and rating scale. Across seven matched decision-model--backbone pairs, decision models are more stable under option-label, irrelevant-information, and rating-scale changes in all seven pairs; six pairs also show lower option-order flip rates. They incur smaller accuracy losses under incorrect external judgments in all seven pairs and conflicting descriptions in six. In six pairs, they gain less accuracy from correct external judgments and show less favorable accuracy changes under consistent descriptions. Among pairs with unchanged semantic decisions, mean absolute changes in answer probabilities range from 4.56 to 11.55 percentage points, revealing input effects that accuracy alone misses.

papers.title: Edge cuts of bounded degree in sparse graphs
papers.summary: Every simple graph on $n \ge 2$ vertices with at most $2n-2$ edges can be split into two nonempty parts with at most two crossing edges at each vertex. For $d \ge 3$ we bound the minimum number of edges in an n-vertex graph without a d-cut.

papers.title: Multiplicative Sidon basis
papers.summary: For a $h \ge 2$ integer a sequence of positive integers $A$ is called asymptotic basis of order $h$ if every sufficiently large positive integer $n$ can be written as a sum of $h$ elements of $A$. We say a sequence of positive integers $A$ is a multiplicative Sidon sequence if all the products of two elements of the sequence $A$ are distinct. In this paper we prove the existence of a multiplicative Sidon set which is an asymptotic basis of order 2 by using the probabilistic method.

papers.title: Twisting Spinning Particles with Superghost Backgrounds
papers.summary: We construct twists of spinning particles in the classical BV formalism by giving constant backgrounds to the bosonic ghosts of local worldline supersymmetry, in analogy with Costello and Li's twist of supergravity, which gives a nonzero background to the ghost of local spacetime supersymmetry. We represent the superghosts on polynomial states and gauge selected worldline R symmetries, imposing the shifted R constraints absolutely and the unshifted ones relatively. On flat targets, the N=2 particle, its N=4 extension on a complex target and an N=8 particle with two fermion flavors give the de Rham, Dolbeault and polynomial linear BCOV complexes. The last two are the linearized field content of the open and closed B-model target-space theories. Pairings and interactions require target-space input beyond the reduced worldline differentials.

papers.title: Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation (ROGUE-AI)
papers.summary: Agents based on large language models (LLMs) can now delete files and send payments on behalf of their users. News media reports routinely describe failures of these agents (e.g., Replit's coding agent deleting a production database), but a report often only says what went wrong and rarely (in)validates the incident or finds its root cause. Incident catalogs collect these reports, and benchmarks record whether agents fail, but neither replicates an incident nor tests the cause its report might identify. In this paper, we present ROGUE-AI (Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation), a multi-agent framework that closes the above gap and rebuilds each reported incident offline together with a matched control that lacks only the blamed cause, and runs agents on both. Our results suggest that ROGUE-AI is able to reproduce the reported harm in 89% of its 108 attempted replications. Agents built on five current GPT, Claude, Gemini and DeepSeek models made the reported mistake in 18% to 33% of runs, against at most 1% without the blamed cause. Of the 72 incidents with real-world harm, 62 had no underlying attacker, and in these, agents did what their task asked for but missed an ordinary hazard, such as a database shared with the live site. Replications without an attacker caused more harm than replications of prompt injection for all five models. Defenses against prompt injection look for injected instructions, but these replications contain none. Further, a warning after each tool output that names the hazard and its consequence lowered harm for all five models, whereas a note of the same length that does not mention the hazard left most of the harm in place. Built from real incidents, the ROGUE-AI replications form a reusable audit framework that vendors can rerun before each new release.
papers.comment: 21 pages, 5 figures, 13 tables. Project page: https://rogue-ai.surge.sh

papers.title: Nematic equilibria on a Möbius strip: topology and extrinsic curvature
papers.summary: We investigate the equilibrium configurations of a nematic liquid crystal confined in a thin tubular neighbourhood of a Möbius strip. Assuming degenerate tangential anchoring and a director uniform across the thickness, we derive an effective two-dimensional Frank energy that accounts for both the intrinsic and extrinsic curvature of the mid-surface. The non-orientability of the substrate imposes identification conditions that couple the reversal of the local frame to the head-to-tail symmetry of the nematic director. We show that the resulting topological classification depends on the parity of the number of half-twists: the sector index is a winding number for even parity, whereas only its parity is physically meaningful for odd parity, in which case the net director rotation is not quantised. We analyse the narrow-strip limit and solve the full two-dimensional equilibrium problem by finite-element methods. The competition between topological sectors depends on the strip aspect ratio and elastic anisotropy. In particular, for a single half-twist, the preferred sector changes at an aspect ratio of approximately 0.58, while for two half-twists two distinct minima of the same sector exchange their energy ordering near 0.60, without any change of topology. These results reveal how non-orientable topology and extrinsic curvature jointly shape nematic equilibria on curved substrates.

papers.title: Chemical Cartography Across Time: The Age-Dependent Chemical Structure of the Milky Way with a Homogeneous Sample of 580,000 Giants from Five Surveys
papers.summary: Mapping the distribution of elements in the Milky Way and understanding how that distribution has changed over time can give us insight into the formation and evolution of our Galaxy. Here we use homogeneously estimated atmospheric parameters, elemental abundances, distances, and ages for ~580,000 giants from five major spectroscopic surveys---all simultaneously placed on a single, self-consistent scale by one model---allowing us, for the first time, to use a large sample of stars with uniform labels and ages that cumulatively span much of the disk to trace how the metallicity structure of the Milky Way depends on stellar age. Our chrono-chemical analysis shows that the radial metallicity gradient of the disk depends non-monotonically on age: it is shallow for the youngest stars, steepening to a maximum of ~-0.07 dex/kpc at intermediate ages (~5-6 Gyr), and flattening to near zero for the oldest stars. This "U-shaped" age dependence is driven largely by the low-alpha (thin-disk) population, with the high-alpha (thick-disk) sequence having weak gradients at all ages. In contrast to [Fe/H], the radial [Mg/Fe] gradient is weak (<~0.01 dex/kpc) at all ages. Together, these trends are consistent with an inside-out formation scenario in which the gradient of the star-forming gas has flattened over at least the last ~6 Gyr, while the near-zero gradient of the oldest stars reflects their formation in a well-mixed disk, efficient radial migration, or both.
papers.comment: 20 pages, 17 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to ApJ

papers.title: Refractive Neutrino Mass: Effects of Fluctuations of the Dark Matter Field
papers.summary: Observed neutrino oscillations can be reproduced by a refractive neutrino mass-squared arising from interactions with ultralight scalar dark matter (ULDM). The wave behaviour of the scalar field gives rise to a fluctuating interference pattern, inducing spatial and temporal variations in the refractive mass that can distort neutrino oscillation probabilities. We simulate the interference patterns of the scalar field in the presence of self-interactions. Using results of these simulations, the oscillation probabilities for JUNO and T2K experiments are computed. We find that the refractive mass scenario remains viable for the complex scalar field without self-coupling for $m_φ\lesssim 10^{-16}~\mathrm{eV}$. For $m_φ\gtrsim10^{-16}~\mathrm{eV}$, repulsive self-interactions narrow the density distribution, reducing the deviation of the survival probability at the first minimum to $ΔP \approx 0.07$ for an appropriate self-interaction coupling. In contrast, for a real scalar field, rapid oscillations with the Compton frequency distort the probabilities for scalar masses $ 10^{-22}~\mathrm{eV} \lesssim m_φ\lesssim 10^{-10} ~\mathrm{eV}$, and self-interactions do not remove this distortion. This distortion becomes negligible only for $m_φ\gtrsim10^{-9}~\mathrm{eV}$. We explore additional effects which could modify the interference pattern and relax the constraints on the required values of $m_φ$. These include scenarios with multiple scalar fields (the axiverse), the gravitational effects of the Sun and Earth on the granule structure, and interactions with the relic neutrino background.

papers.title: Demographic inference in exoplanet chemistry is shaped by retrieval assumptions
papers.summary: Understanding the chemical diversity of exoplanet atmospheres is crucial for linking atmospheric composition to planetary formation history. Atmospheric C/O can provide clues about where and how planets form, particularly through the accretion of gas and solids across disk snowlines. Since planetary migration can change orbital distances and hence equilibrium temperatures ($T_{eq}$), investigating C/O across different planetary populations may provide insights into their formation and evolution. As observational precision improves with the JWST, the limits of standard atmospheric retrieval methods that assume altitude-independent molecular abundances have become apparent. We present atmospheric retrievals for 20 transiting planets with published JWST transmission spectra, including complementary HST spectra for targets where such data are available, spanning gas giants, warm Neptunes, and temperate/warm sub-Neptunes, to test how population-level chemical inferences depend on retrieval assumptions. Free-chemistry retrievals show a visually non-monotonic C/O-$T_{eq}$ distribution, but this apparent pattern is not statistically robust and is sensitive to sample composition. When molecular abundances are constrained by a grid of disequilibrium models, the inferred C/O distribution becomes more restricted, showing that demographic chemical trends can depend strongly on the adopted retrieval parameterization. Several hot Jupiters converge to low C/O ($\leq$ 0.05), whereas colder, cloudy planets retain broad posteriors that reflect limited information content of their spectra. Our results suggest that population-level chemical trends inferred from free-chemistry retrievals should be interpreted with caution unless sample selection, residual structure, prior sensitivity, and chemical assumptions are explicitly tested.
papers.comment: 52 Figures, 10 Tables, Accepted in Communications Chemistry

papers.title: Nonlinearly Causal General-Relativistic Superfluid Hydrodynamics: Simulating Vortex Dynamics in Neutron-Star Interiors
papers.summary: Neutron stars provide a natural laboratory for superfluid matter under extreme conditions. Its nonlinear dynamics is central to pulsar glitches, their possible links to fast radio bursts, and tidal interactions in inspiralling binaries. We develop a general-relativistic superfluid hydrodynamics framework incorporating entrainment, vortex forces, and line energy, and derive, for the first time, necessary and sufficient conditions for nonlinear causality and strong hyperbolicity. We also show that commonly used dissipative, force-balanced formulations without line tension are generically ill-posed at short wavelengths because of the Donnelly-Glaberson instability. Exploiting the analogy between vortex arrays with tension and force-free electrodynamics, we recast vortex dynamics in terms of effective electric and magnetic fields and drift velocities. This motivates a new finite-volume scheme combining constrained transport of superfluid vorticity with implicit electric-field evolution, enabling stable numerical evolution of the full system. We validate the scheme using an exact solution to the relativistic superfluid Riemann problem and Kelvin-wave dispersion relations, among other tests. Finally, we simulate dynamical, global general-relativistic two-fluid neutron-star equilibria, validate their oscillation modes, and present the first simplified calculation of superfluid interior spin-down with prescribed vortex release and repinning. The resulting stationary state retains both a net twist in the vortex array and residual differential rotation of the superfluid. Our framework thus enables nonlinear numerical studies of general-relativistic superfluid dynamics in neutron-star interiors.

papers.title: A time-domain adversarial example demonstrating the failure of $H^1$ elements in $a$-$φ$ electromagnetic simulation
papers.summary: Frequently, $H^1$ continuous finite elements are used in computational electromagnetics despite it being widely known that such an interpolation is not guaranteed to furnish reliable approximations of solutions to general initial/boundary value problems. It is mathematically more natural to use $H(\text{Curl})$ elements (edge elements) than $H^1$ elements, since the former form part of a discrete complex that respects the differential-geometric structure of Maxwell's equations while the latter do not. However, most work discussing the failure of $H^1$ elements for electromagnetics is esoteric and concrete examples demonstrating the clear advantage of edge elements are generally restricted to quasi-static, frequency-domain, or eigenvalue problems. In this work, we summarize essential facts regarding $H^1$ and $H(\text{Curl})$ elements and present a physically feasible yet intentionally adversarial time-domain eddy-current example demonstrating the failure of gauge-penalized $H^1$ elements in an $a$-$φ$ formulation compared to gauge-free mixed scalar/edge $H^1/H(\text{Curl})$ elements. The results indicate that edge elements can be used to furnish reasonable results for general loading conditions, whereas penalized $H^1$ elements fail (e.g., converge to an incorrect state) even with mesh refinement.

papers.title: The Geometry of Lies: Knowledge and Persona Directions for Detecting Deception in Large Language Models
papers.summary: Linear probes are the cheapest LLM lie detectors but often fail to transfer across kinds of lie. Label-free directions from honest and deceptive role-play are untested at 70B scale and on lies about knowledge, where a lie and an honest denial can be identical. We widen a published persona bank with roles that deny knowledge they have, plus honest counterparts. At each model's middle layer the resulting persona direction ranks lies across Liars' Bench better than single-dataset probes on three of its four models; it fails on Qwen, even when Qwen stays in role far more often. On Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct it beats directions from a random persona bank, but its gain over the published direction is within the range of random widenings. On lies about knowledge, persona directions mainly track a reply's wording: where lies and honest denials share their words, our three main contrasts stay inside the random-direction band on Llama and Qwen and reach only its edge on Gemma, though on Mistral one clears it. A knowledge direction contrasts questions the model can answer with ones nobody can, each followed by the same scripted denial. It separates lies from identical honest denials on two models and narrowly on a third, but not on the fourth; its other results partly depend on the benchmark's wording. On the Gender-Secret fine-tune it clears the band by a few hundredths on Llama and fails on Mistral. The sum of the two directions ranks lies better than a supervised probe at the same depth on all four models (on one, both near chance) but is level with the persona direction on Llama's average and behind that probe on held-out lies. More varied role-play questions do not help the persona direction on Liars' Bench.

papers.title: Pathwise uniqueness for the stochastic heat equation with a $3/4$-Hölder diffusion coefficient
papers.summary: For every $γ\in[3/4,1]$, we prove pathwise uniqueness and strong existence for the stochastic heat equation on $\mathbb{R}$ with space-time white noise, Lipschitz drift, and a diffusion coefficient locally $γ$-Hölder under suitable growth bounds. The result settles the critical case $γ=3/4$ left open by Mueller, Mytnik and Perkins. The proof is based on a newly developed short-time linear comparison method. On each short interval, we compare the difference of two solutions with an auxiliary linear process. An expected weighted $L^1$ bound independent of the noise multiplier, together with a vanishing sum of approximation errors, yields pathwise uniqueness. The method may also apply to other SPDEs admitting analogous linear comparison and stochastic convolution estimates.

papers.title: Minimization of free energy in a Poisson--Boltzmann problem
papers.summary: In this paper, we study a mathematical model in which an ionic solution composed of several types of spherical ions is confined between two uniformly charged parallel planes. The ion concentrations at equilibrium, determined by the interplay between thermal and electrostatic effects, are obtained by minimizing the free energy of the system. The resulting minimization problem is infinite-dimensional, and we prove the existence and uniqueness of its solution by means of a norm-convergence direct method based on the Banach--Saks property of the space in which the problem is posed. The existence proof is technically challenging because the functional to be minimized is not coercive in general. Three illustrative problems are considered and solved numerically.

papers.title: Authenticating quantum key distribution through random position checks
papers.summary: Quantum key distribution (QKD) requires some form of authentication in order for the parties to be sure they are not unknowingly generating a key with an adversary pretending to be one of the honest parties. In this work, we propose a protocol in which the position of one of the parties is used as the authentication credential for key distribution. Our protocol essentially consists of a BB84 QKD protocol with quantum position verification (QPV) rounds randomly interleaved in. The approach is efficient compared with previous approaches, which required running an entire QPV protocol for every bit requiring authentication. We undertake an initial security analysis of the protocol for a restricted set of attacks.

papers.title: Self-gravity depletes superradiant clouds
papers.summary: Superradiant clouds of ultralight scalars around black holes are often modeled as free fields, whose levels grow independently and decay slowly through gravitational-wave emission. We show that this limit is never realized. The cloud's self-gravity redistributes particles between levels, just as in the case of axion self-interactions, and dominates over self-interactions for decay constants $f_a\gtrsim6\times10^{16}\,{\rm GeV}\,(α/0.1)$, with $α$ the gravitational fine-structure constant. Self-gravity depletes the cloud by orders of magnitude and feeds more extended levels, weakening all signals that rely on the existence of a large cloud mass. A binary companion, however, can partly offset the depletion. Any assessment of superradiant signals must therefore account for both self-gravity and the cloud's environment.

papers.title: AURA: AUdio-dRiven streaming Avatar
papers.summary: Current audio-driven video diffusion models can synthesize realistic talking-head videos but generally require dozens of diffusion denoising steps over multi-second video chunks, making them unsuitable for streaming applications such as voice assistants and virtual avatars, where low-latency and online causal generation are required properties. AURA generates video chunk by chunk with a rolling KV cache, requiring only the audio of the current chunk to start generating, rather than a multi-second audio look-ahead like bidirectional models. It comes in two sizes: AURA 1.3B streams 576p video in real time on a single GPU (20.7 fps for a 16 Hz playback rate), making it suited to interactive avatar applications, and AURA 5B streams 720p video at 9.7 fps. Our two-stage distillation pipeline first aligns the causal student with the teacher, by training it to match the teacher's trajectories with fewer diffusion steps and a chunk-wise sliding window causal attention mask, then applies Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) with backward simulation to close the remaining quality gap. On standard talking-head benchmarks, AURA 1.3B runs 23x faster than its own bidirectional teacher and reaches a quality comparable to TalkVerse at a lower resolution, and AURA 5B matches its TalkVerse teacher at 720p while running 17x faster. To support reproducibility and further research on streaming avatar generation, we release the weights of both models along with a dataset of 30K synthetic videos and their precomputed teacher trajectories.

papers.title: Large $k$-cross-free families
papers.summary: Two subsets $A,B$ of a finite set $X$ are crossing if $A\cap B$, $A\setminus B$, $B\setminus A$, and $X\setminus(A\cup B)$ are all nonempty. A family is $k$-cross-free if it contains no $k$ pairwise crossing members. We construct such families on $n$ elements of size $(\frac{1}{3}+o(1))kn\log k$, where the asymptotic is taken as $k$ tends to infinity and is uniform over all integers $n\ge k$. This disproves the uniform $O(kn)$ bound conjectured by Karzanov and Lomonosov. Our construction consists of cyclic intervals with at most one point deleted, together with their complements. We also prove an $O(kn\log k)$ upper bound for $k$-cross-free families closed under all cyclic shifts of a fixed cyclic ordering of the ground set.

papers.title: LLM GerryMandering: Separating Interactions from Additive Effects in LLM Audits
papers.summary: Intersectional bias arises when a model treats people who hold several marginalised identities at once differently from what their separate identities would predict. Auditing such intersectional subgroups remains a challenge: their number grows quadratically, and there is no agreed baseline for what independent attributes would predict. Without such a baseline, many existing audits flag a subgroup when it exceeds each attribute alone, a condition that attributes acting independently already satisfy. We test this standard criterion on 150 synthetic datasets built with no interaction. With the shuffle null, it flags 66.1 false subgroups per dataset on average, and at least one in every dataset. When we plant interactions of known size into these datasets, a repaired null lets the criterion recover only 32% of them. We introduce ADDIS (Additive Intersectional Screen), which fits an additive model over all attributes, scores each subgroup by its Additive Residual Distance (ARD) from that model's prediction, and tests it against a Freedman-Lane null. On our synthetic benchmark, ADDIS flags 0.09 false subgroups per dataset and recovers 84% of the same planted interactions. We then build IndiPersona, 10,000 synthetic Indian personas with six identity attributes, and audit 13 open language models. The standard criterion flags 7.1% of the 738 tested subgroups on average; ADDIS flags 3.0%. Gender identity crossed with sexual orientation is the largest pairing in every model, and counterfactual personas confirm it and additionally reveal a caste x class interaction in all but one model that the observational test lacked the data to detect. Much of what audits report as intersectional bias can thus arise from independent single-attribute effects alone, yet a small core of interactions survives.

papers.title: On the design of sequential quantum repeaters with error detection
papers.summary: Long-distance, trust-free quantum communications rely on the development of scalable quantum repeater schemes. Sequential entanglement generation with error detection is a promising approach that combines manageable implementation requirements with a hop-by-hop architecture compatible with existing classical infrastructure. In this paper, we investigate key design choices for such schemes over a repeater chain using quantum key distribution as a benchmark. We find that simple quantum error-detecting codes, such as repetition codes or quantum parity codes, perform well under near-term hardware assumptions and outperform strategies without any encoding. In particular, we show that two-qubit repetition codes may well be all that we need to implement in many practical scenarios. We also examine different architectures for the generation of initial entanglement and assess their merits. Additionally, we show that moderate improvements in some hardware components can partially mitigate the slow technological progress of others.

papers.title: Anytime-valid inference for time series via self-normalization
papers.summary: We develop a self-normalized approach to constructing asymptotic confidence sequences for a broad class of parameters of stationary time series under weak dependence. Our theory covers nonlinear marginal parameters, including quantiles, expectiles and expected shortfall, as well as autoregressive coefficients. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first use of self-normalization to construct asymptotic confidence sequences for time series. A key advantage is that the construction avoids direct estimation of the long-run variance, which can be particularly challenging for nonlinear parameters under serial dependence. Following an initial burn-in period of length $m$, confidence intervals are released sequentially, with simultaneous coverage over all subsequent times converging to $1-α$ as $m\to\infty$. We propose two sequential self-normalizers with complementary statistical and computational advantages. The forward construction uses only the history of sequential parameter estimates, leading to minimal computational overhead. The three-block construction typically yields narrower confidence sequences and is compatible with the optimal law-of-the-iterated-logarithm width rate. Together, these constructions extend the benefits of self-normalization to sequential inference under dependence. We investigate their finite-sample performance through simulations and illustrate their use in Markov chain Monte Carlo output analysis in the supplementary appendix.

papers.title: Outflow Properties from a Broad Range of GR$ν$RMHD Stellar-Mass Black Hole Accretion Disks
papers.summary: The majority of the mass ejected by neutron star mergers comes from accretion disk outflows. Over timescales of seconds, the thermodynamic evolution of the disk and its resultant outflows set the stage for the ejecta properties which manifest in kilonova observations at later times (hours/days). Kilonova observables depend sensitively on key properties of these outflows -- mass ejection, the ejecta velocity distribution, late-time ejecta morphology and nucleosynthetic yields -- which can only be modeled with a detailed treatment of microphysical interactions including neutrino and general relativistic effects. In this work, we present a library of 25 general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic accretion disks with neutrino transport, to our knowledge the largest to date, spanning a broad range of black hole and accretion disk combinations. From fits to our simulations, we derive analytic estimates of the average ejecta velocity distribution and mass ejection both at simulation end and extrapolated out to the end of the disk's lifetime. We also report ejecta morphology at timescales relevant to kilonova modeling, present spatially-dependent nucleosynthetic yields, and discuss the latter's dependence on initial disk conditions. While our disk library primarily includes initial conditions expected after neutron star mergers, a subset of our disks are applicable to other kilonova-adjacent scenarios.

papers.title: Emergent Fatigue Dynamics from Foundational Interatomic Potentials
papers.summary: Foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials are trained on large, diverse DFT datasets, but their validation rests on equilibrium states, which does not guarantee correct emergent behavior in large-scale molecular dynamics. Where no direct experimental validation is available, comparisons to physically motivated potentials are valuable for drawing insight. We distinguish static properties, which are thermally accessible, from emergent properties, which require work from an external fatigue stress to drive rare events, and compare the potentials on both. An EAM potential and the NequIP foundational potential both agree closely with reference data for many near-equilibrium properties, but NequIP predicts an anomalously low intrinsic stacking fault energy ($\sim7$ times lower than EAM) and thus predicts far more plastic deformation under fatigue cycling of a nanoscale flaw modeled after the classical Griffith crack problem. Per-atom energy distributions after loading show that the two potentials differ most at energies far above what is thermally accessible. We also document memory-related crashes and silent extrapolation as practical concerns for practitioners of these foundational model forms.

papers.title: From power to spectrum: an off-the-shelf photodiode turned into a spectrometer by its bias alone
papers.summary: Computational spectrometers replace dispersive optics with detectors whose spectral response can be varied, but every reported single-detector device obtains this response through dedicated fabrication: two-dimensional heterostructures, graded epitaxial junctions, organic stacks, filters or photonic circuits. We demonstrate a generic, fabrication-free alternative in which a standard commercial photodiode becomes a spectrometer through its electrical drive alone, requiring no modification of the device, no optical filter and no modulation of the light. The mechanism is bias-modulated optoelectronic chromatic dispersion (OED): light of different wavelengths is absorbed at different depths, and a sinusoidal bias changes how carriers generated at each depth are collected, so that every spectrum is encoded in the shape of the photocurrent waveform over one bias period. Applied to an unmodified InGaAs PIN photodiode at room temperature, a 10 us waveform decoded by a neural network reconstructs spectra of one to three laser lines across the 80 nm of the telecom C+L band, locating the lines to 0.3-0.4 nm, counting them in about 99% of measurements and identifying their power levels, with line shifts tracked to tens of picometres. Because OED relies on universal semiconductor transport physics, the approach is material-agnostic and applies in principle to any off-the-shelf photodiode, turning detectors already deployed as power monitors into low-cost spectral sensors.

papers.title: Cost-Aware Agentic Feature Optimization System for Fleet-Scale Ranking Models
papers.summary: Large Web platforms operate large fleets of ranking models, each selecting features from a shared pool of tens of thousands. We present an end-to-end agentic system that optimizes features across the fleet under resource constraints shared across models and those set per model, such as feature pipeline cost and serving throughput (QPS), respectively. In this system, LLM agents propose hypotheses, and deterministic tools execute experiments and verify them. For each model, an LLM generates and shortlists cross features from a combinatorial candidate space, and all features are then ranked by several importance methods. Feature blending mixes these rankings into a single selection, using Pareto fronts across tasks for multi-task models. An LLM Researcher agent then tunes the feature selection in 10--25 asynchronous trials under resource caps, and a trimming step keeps the pipeline cost within budget. Across production models, the system improves normalized entropy by 0.31% on average within each model's budget, and the trimming step cuts pipeline cost by 2.3% with no regression beyond measurement noise. The optimized models were launched, and in online A/B tests they improved a primary online metric by 0.20%.

papers.title: Full Kummer Beams: Skyrmionic textures in bichromatic light
papers.summary: In this work, we introduce full Kummer beams, the bichromatic analog of full Poincaré beams. To this end, we define three parameters that characterize bichromatic states of polarization and span the Kummer shape, the bichromatic counterpart of the Poincaré sphere. We find that, under certain conditions, full Kummer beams can exhibit skyrmionic textures with a Skyrme number that depends not only on the topological charges but also on the frequencies. These beams can also exhibit emergent behavior upon propagation, including robust, higher-order-like structures and a propagation-invariant Skyrme number over a wide range of beam-waist selections.

papers.title: Exact fermionic decay length and Majorana localization in the sign-alternating kagomé Ising model
papers.summary: We derive an exact fermionic decay length for the sign-alternating kagomé Ising model at fixed transverse momentum $p=π/2$. Writing $x=\tanh K_1$, $y=\tanh K_2$, and $z=\tanh K_3$ for the three dimensionless couplings, the inverse length per lattice cell is $ξ_{\rm f}^{-1}=|\ln(U/|V|)|$, where $U=(1-x^2)(1+y^2z^2)$ and $V=(1+x^2)(y^2-z^2)$. The length diverges at $U=|V|$, with the sign of $V$ selecting one of two classical critical branches. In a simultaneous strong- and weak-bond scaling, these branches become the gap-closing conditions at momenta $0$ and $π$ of the transverse-field Ising chain obtained from the row transfer matrix. On the topological side, the classical decay length tends to the localization length of a Majorana end mode of the Jordan--Wigner fermion chain. We also prove that the regular strong-bond Yang--Baxter family cannot be continued to the finite-coupling interior within the fixed-basis ansatz with one vanishing bond direction.

papers.title: Constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Finite Element Model Updating: Closed-Form Hyperelastic Strain Energies from Heterogeneous Experiments
papers.summary: Calibrating a hyperelastic constitutive model for a soft material traditionally poses two problems: an expert must choose its functional form, and several homogeneous tests must determine its parameters. Neural constitutive models solve the first, but either remain black boxes or draw on a library of candidate terms fixed in advance. Full-field measurements, such as those from digital image correlation (DIC), promise to solve the second, replacing those tests by a single heterogeneous one. Two gaps remain: flexibility during training with interpretability afterwards, and a way to train such a model on one heterogeneous test. Here we close both. We embed a constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold network (CKAN) in finite element model updating (FEMU) and train it by minimizing the mismatch between the predicted and the measured kinematic fields and reaction forces. Pruning and symbolic regression then reduce the trained network to a compact closed-form strain energy that satisfies every constitutive requirement. On perforated natural-rubber membranes, the CKANs reproduce the DIC displacement fields with median errors between one and two percent, and transfer to a hole pattern withheld from training. On a perforated silicone plate, a CKAN trained on one stretch profile at a single load reproduces that profile and the measured reaction force to within a few percent. On an aortic specimen inflated under pressure, an anisotropic CKAN predicts the inflated three-dimensional shape. The discovered closed-form energies match the CKANs they replace on the training data and can be compared directly with established models.

papers.title: Thermal-Guided Ensemble Reinforcement Learning for Regime-Adaptive Short-Term GPU Power Forecasting in AI Data Centers
papers.summary: AI data centers (AIDCs) introduce bursty and regime-dependent load patterns, posing significant challenges for reliable energy management and predictive grid control. To address these challenges, this letter proposes a thermal-guided ensemble reinforcement learning framework for probabilistic AIDC load forecasting. A soft actor-critic (SAC) agent with a simplex-preserving policy adaptively weights LSTM, TCN, and Transformer predictors at every time step based on their realized errors. A thermal-guided neural correction estimates the ensemble residual, while a sensitivity-projection regularizer enforces the non-negative sensitivity of power to GPU utilization and temperature. The corrected ensemble output is further processed by a Bayesian probabilistic layer to produce predictive distributions and quantify forecasting uncertainty. Case studies on 1-second MIT Supercloud telemetry show that the proposed method reduces the normalized mean absolute error to about 1% across all computing regimes, compared with 4-11% for deep learning-based and ensemble learning benchmarks, and converges faster with narrower prediction intervals than a DRL ensemble without thermal guidance.

papers.title: Backtracking Agent Applications Security Incidents
papers.summary: Agent applications are increasingly deployed, yet agent-specific attacks pose real threats to them. Upon a security incident, organizations backtrack to identify the CEP (compromise entry point), remediate the damage, and prevent its recurrence. The main artifacts available for backtracking are trajectory logs, which record agent functionalities, and source code; app(lication)-specific function call logs are often fairly limited. However, trajectory logs are at the agent functionality abstraction layer, while the CEP candidates are function calls at the app code execution layer. Due to this semantic gap, the analyst needs to manually inspect the relevant code for each CEP candidate to infer its corresponding agent functionality. In this work, we present Origin, a backtracking tool for the analyst to submit a small number of queries to identify CEPs that existing tools cannot provide. Our approach poses two challenges: (1) define the intermediate abstraction that captures the mapping relationships between the two semantic layers; (2) determine the region-to-variable mapping for constructing the cross-layer graph defined in the intermediate abstraction. Each region is a specific group of agent functionalities. Origin addresses the challenges by (1) the cross-layer dependency graph (CLDG) that connects region-inferred functions at the semantic level to the variables in the low-level taint propagation subgraph, plus the associated query language, and (2) the region inference algorithm. Case studies on five popular agent applications across eight attack incidents show that an analyst using Origin correctly identifies all the CEPs.
papers.comment: 33 pages (12 pages of main text, 3 pages of references, 18 pages of appendices), 9 figures, 12 tables

papers.title: Hamiltonian Stabilization of the Two-Photon Dicke Model
papers.summary: Collective two-photon light--matter interactions enable pair amplification but can destroy spectral confinement, preventing a stable thermodynamic bright phase. We show that a positive Kac-scaled number-Kerr interaction renders the two-photon Dicke Hamiltonian of \(N\) emitters lower-bounded at all couplings while preserving its generalized \(\mathbb Z_4\) symmetry. We determine the exact zero-temperature thermodynamic energy density with \(O(N^{-1})\) finite-size control and obtain the global phase diagram. A bright minimum is born at a saddle-node and exchanges global stability with the normal minimum at coexistence, producing a discontinuous photon-density jump. Symmetry-resolved exact diagonalization through \(N=128\) supports the predicted density jump and an exponentially closing same-sector normal--bright tunneling gap. Spectral collapse thus becomes the singular zero-Kerr point of a first-order phase diagram, identifying a Hamiltonian route to stabilizing pair amplification.

papers.title: Deterministic Temporal Embedding for Calcium Imaging Trace Extraction
papers.summary: Reliable extraction of calcium-dependent fluorescence traces in calcium imaging sequences requires identifying pixels whose fluorescence intensity reflects the same underlying cellular activity. We present a deterministic temporal embedding framework that maps pixel-wise fluorescence traces to a low-dimensional representation in which temporally coherent sources form spatially coherent regions. Starting from a fuzzy-neighborhood graph and spectral initialization, we optimize a class-balanced cross-entropy objective using exact sparse attraction and a deterministic particle-mesh decomposition of the dense repulsive interaction with sparse edge compensation, avoiding stochastic negative sampling. The resulting latent representation is spatially decoded into reliable source supports for trace extraction without imposing an explicit cellular shape prior. Experiments on synthetic and in vivo two-photon calcium imaging data demonstrate robust recovery of irregular and spatially touching sources together with efficient deterministic embedding optimization.

papers.title: The Window Lever: Longer Observation Windows Outweigh the Observed Effects of Data, Capacity, and Architecture in Customer Behavior Forecasting
papers.summary: In our experiments on long-horizon customer-behavior forecasting, a longer observation window outweighed the observed effects of more data, more capacity and newer architectures. The window is the weeks of history a model sees before the week it forecasts from. Going from an 8- to a 16-week window adds a raw +0.070 to 0.107 log-space $R^2$ in every family at 1M. Matched test cohorts, which score the same customer-weeks at every window, show this raw comparison understates the gain in every family they cover. The direction holds on five public datasets, four spanning over a year (ridge and our transformer on all five). On our internal data, longer windows admit up to 10% more and colder training customers, which matching does not fix. Our design does not separate window length from calendar coverage, because every test anchor (the week a forecast is made from) falls in one eight-week band. On training-period anchors, the weekly ridge probe's gain persists outside the holiday season, keeping about 72% of it. We therefore report a robust positive association with longer windows and do not identify the magnitude of a calendar-independent history effect. Of four internally registered predictions, the only fully blind one failed. An activity-mixture model predicted +0.014 from 24 to 32 weeks; the weekly-aggregate probe returned -0.0004. For the sequence families, the other three levers are about an order of magnitude smaller, bounded and unresolved. Their observed effects are at most 0.006 between the nominal 1M and 10M tiers and 0.0052 among five sequence families at 16 weeks with clocks as built, both single-seed on the full test split, and 0.006 for capacity on three-seed means. These are observed intervals, not equivalence bounds. Our claim is the order-of-magnitude contrast between the window and those bounds. A team building on this class of data should start by lengthening the window.

papers.title: $Zγ$ production in gluon fusion at NLO+NLL
papers.summary: We study the production of $Zγ$ in gluon fusion at hadron colliders at the next-to-leading-order (NLO) in QCD. At the $13.6$ TeV LHC, we find that these NLO corrections are found to enhance the leading-order (LO) cross section by about $83$\% and reduce the conventional seven-point scale uncertainty from $22.3$\% at LO to $15.2$\% at NLO. We further perform the threshold resummation at next-to-leading-logarithmic (NLL) accuracy and match to the fixed order NLO results. We have presented the production cross section for various center of mass energies at the LHC. We find that this NLL resummation enhances the NLO production cross section by about $23$\%. We also give the invariant mass distribution up to $Q=1000$ GeV for $13.6$ TeV LHC. In this case, the resummation reduces the seven-point scale uncertainty from $25\%$ at NLO to about $16$\% at NLO+NLL for $Q=1000$ GeV. We also present the uncertainties due to the strong coupling constant and the parton distribution functions in our results. We further estimate the contribution of the top quark in our predictions, using the Born Improved Theory (BIT).

papers.title: ACE-Brain-0.7: Learning Execution-Grounded Reasoning for Embodied Agents
papers.summary: Reliable reasoning for long-horizon embodied tasks requires predictions grounded in the observed execution state. We present ACE-Brain-0.7, a 9B vision--language model that combines spatial grounding, task understanding, and progress estimation. To train the model, we curate 3.7 million question--answer pairs, drawing execution supervision from egocentric human videos, robot episodes, and simulation. These questions span different stages of an execution and connect task-level judgments with observed progress and outcomes. We then fine-tune Qwen3.5-9B on this collection together with additional task, spatial-grounding, and progress-estimation data. Across six public task-reasoning benchmarks, ACE-Brain-0.7 achieves an average score of 76.5, ahead of GPT-6 Astra at 72.7 and Claude Opus 5.5 at 73.5. Our model also leads the evaluated models in spatial grounding, averaging 75.90 across seven benchmarks and reaching 91.25 Acc@0.5 on RefCOCOg. Controlled evaluations further indicate that our task-only model makes more effective use of visual history and more accurately distinguishes execution states. Together, these results show that ACE-Brain-0.7 effectively combines spatial perception with temporal understanding, delivering strong execution-grounded reasoning and comparing favorably with closed-source models.

papers.title: Plan4D: Generative Plannable 4D Worlds
papers.summary: Most world models for future prediction prioritize aestetic quality of generated videos, but offer only weak physical grounding and limited geometric consistency over time, due to the lack of explicit 4D modeling. In this paper, we introduce plan4d, a possible next milestone towards building a generative plannable 4D world model that predicts future RGB videos together with dense 4D geometry, including depth, cameras, point clouds, and scene flow from an observed scene context and text-specified actions. Since training data with paired actions and dense 4D annotations is inherently scarce, plan4d leverages the complementary priors of foundational video generators and 3D reconstructors. Specifically, we propose a model-stitching architecture that couples Depth Anything 3 with LongCat-Video and augments it with an auxiliary DPT head for scene-flow prediction. The resulting model allows us to plan and generate complex, long-horizon, and fine-grained actions in a dynamic 3D scenes, while substantially improving both visual fidelity and geometric accuracy of the generated future videos. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that plan4d achieves state-of-the-art performance in generative 4D modeling of environmental reactions. Project Page: https://fogradio.github.io/plan4d-project

papers.title: Simple Private Noisy SGD is Minimax-Optimal under Population Strong Convexity
papers.summary: Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) is at the center of modern machine learning and is known to be statistically minimax-optimal in many regression settings, e.g., for convex Generalized Linear Models (GLMs). Yet, it is unknown whether its simplest differentially private Noisy SGD counterpart fulfills similar favorable guarantees even on strongly convex losses. We resolve this question affirmatively. We upper bound the parameter estimation error for a single pass of Noisy SGD with a fixed stepsize schedule and constant batch sizes on smooth and strongly convex Lipschitz losses over a compact convex domain under Renyi DP. Specialized to strongly convex GLMs, our error bounds match minimax lower bounds we derive based on the Score Attack framework. In particular, this provides the first minimax-optimal rate for Noisy SGD in private logistic regression, avoiding poly-logarithmic terms present in existing results. Our analysis is versatile as it relies on standard convex analysis and establishes the same rates in expectation and with high probability.

papers.title: Hybrid Retrieval for Government Scheme Search in English and Marathi
papers.summary: Retrieving government schemes requires matching citizens' information needs to formal administrative descriptions, often across languages and terminology. We present a bilingual search system for Maharashtra government schemes and public services that combines BM25 retrieval with sentence-embedding similarity through equal-weight score fusion. The system indexes aligned English-Marathi scheme descriptions and supports multilingual, Marathi-focused, and translation-mediated semantic configurations. Evaluation on manually curated bilingual queries compares BM25, dense retrieval, and hybrid retrieval using IndicSBERT and MahaSBERT. BM25 provides a strong baseline with a mean reciprocal rank (MRR) of 0.864. Hybrid retrieval increases MRR to 0.872 with IndicSBERT and 0.879 with MahaSBERT, whereas the corresponding dense-only systems achieve 0.663 and 0.655. MahaSBERT-based fusion also increases precision from 0.781 to 0.808 while matching BM25 recall at 0.946. These results support the complementary use of lexical and semantic signals in this collection, while showing that improvements over a strong lexical baseline are modest and metric-dependent. The study provides an application-focused analysis of hybrid retrieval for bilingual public-service information access.

papers.title: Hypergraph Hajnal-Szemerédi
papers.summary: A seminal result of Hajnal and Szemerédi from 1970 asserts that every graph on $n$ vertices with $q\;|\;n$ and minimum degree at least $\Big(1-\frac{1}{q}\Big)n$ admits a $K_q$-factor (a collection of vertex-disjoint copies of $K_q$ spanning all vertices). There has been sustained interest in extending this result to hypergraph $K_q^r$-factors. For general $q$ and $r$, Lu and Székely in 2007 showed that every large enough, $r$-graph $G$ with $q\mid v(G)$ and $δ_{r-1}(G) \ge \left(1- \frac{c}{q^{r-1}}\right)v(G)$ admits a $K_q^r$-factor (where $c$ is a constant depending on $r$ but not $q$), and there have been various subsequent improvements to the constant (but not the order) of this bound over the ensuing decades. Meanwhile, results from codegree Turán theory show that $δ_{r-1}(G) \ge \left(1 - \frac{c \cdot \log q}{q^{r-1}} \right)v(G)$ is necessary. Surprisingly, our main result shows that the order of this upper bound is not correct and, in fact, the codegree $K_q^r$-factor threshold is much closer to this codegree Turán theory bound. In particular, we show that $δ_{r-1}(G) \ge \left( 1-c\cdot \frac{\log^{1-1/(r-1)}q}{q^{r-1}}\right)v(G)$ suffices for the existence of a $K_q^r$-factor. Our key contribution is showing the same is true for the fractional threshold. Inspired by the first and fourth author's recent proof of the Nash-Williams' Conjecture, we accomplish this by combining a linear programming framework with ideas from discharging. Additionally, we establish a technical result about finding large independent sets in sparse, non-uniform hypergraphs, which may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Decision Age: Information Freshness under Fusion Rules in Multi-Sensor Command and Control
papers.summary: Command and control systems decide automatically on evidence that a fusion rule requires from several sensors. The Age of Information measures how current a datum is when it reaches the fusion node, but existing multi-source results treat additional sources as redundancy: the age at the monitor falls as sources are added. This paper addresses the opposite regime. When a rule demands corroboration the decision waits for the slowest required source, so the binding quantity is a maximum, not a minimum, of source ages. We define the decision age of an arbitrary monotone fusion rule, obtain its distribution in closed form for periodic and event-driven sources, and show that the mean decision age grows linearly with the corroboration level, from the floor of the age sawtooth to its peak. We add a dominance criterion that identifies which sensor governs decision freshness, and a measurement methodology for fielded systems. Freshness becomes a verifiable requirement, and adding sensors is shown to make automatic decisions older rather than fresher.

papers.title: Direct3D-V3: Latent-Free Diffusion Transformers in the Native Voxel Domain
papers.summary: Native 3D generation has largely been built around latent diffusion, with recent advances concentrating on stronger variational autoencoders (VAE) and increasingly elaborate latent representations, from vecset and triplanes to structured sparse voxels. Despite their architectural differences, these methods all share the same premise: geometry is first compressed into a latent space and only then modeled by the generator. We take a different route and propose Direct3D-V3, a latent-free diffusion transformer (DiT) framework that discards the VAE altogether and operates in the native voxel domain, directly modeling raw SDF voxel grids during both training and sampling. To make this direct voxel formulation geometrically reliable, we introduce an implicit manifold regularization over neighboring voxels to suppress non-watertight surfaces, and convert predicted SDF grids into meshes via Marching Cubes so that rendered normal losses can supervise the model directly from its predicted SDF. To improve alignment between the conditioning image and generated geometry, Direct3D-V3 also predicts the camera parameters of the conditioning image as an auxiliary task, encouraging the DiT to learn the mapping from image observations to 3D shape. This latent-free design removes the reconstruction bottleneck, brings training under an objective in the native voxel domain, and yields meshes with substantially richer local detail. The predicted camera and native SDF voxel output further make Direct3D-V3 extensible to generative reconstruction, where diffusion is interleaved with normal-guided refinement to improve alignment with the observed view while the generative prior completes unseen regions. Project page: https://dreamtechai.github.io/Direct3D-V3.
papers.comment: The Project Page is: https://dreamtechai.github.io/Direct3D-V3. The Paper is published in ACM TOG (SIGGRAPH Asia 2026)

papers.title: AutoMaster: Autonomous Post-Training by Making the Same Model a Better Teacher
papers.summary: Task success alone does not specify which behaviors post-training should reinforce. Even successful teacher trajectories can contain unsupported assumptions, unproductive repetition, or superficial verification. We propose Skill-FT (Skill-Guided Fine-Tuning), which uses natural-language skills to suppress undesirable habits and elicit underrepresented effective behaviors during teacher rollouts, then fine-tunes a target model on the resulting trajectories. We introduce AutoMaster, an autonomous post-training system in which an LLM agent develops these interventions through trajectory analysis, skill design, data selection, and feedback from rollouts and target-model evaluation. Across Terminal, Search, and software engineering tasks with 4B and 9B target models, AutoMaster improves mean performance over Vanilla SFT on successful unguided teacher trajectories by 1.42-8.99 percentage points, with the teacher, task pool, training set size, and SFT recipe held fixed. Together with the ablations and trajectory analyses, these results suggest that behavioral shaping can make a fixed model a more effective teacher. We further find that retaining skill instructions during SFT yields higher mean performance than removing them across all six settings, despite their absence at evaluation and identical supervised outputs. These findings suggest that preserving skill context as part of a training demonstration can support better behavioral internalization.

papers.title: GLiDE: A Fast, Calibrated Decision Model Distilled from Reasoning Teachers
papers.summary: Decision models enable fast, confidence-aware decisions by scoring candidate answers in a single forward pass, without generating text or intermediate reasoning. Yet reasoning can substantially improve decision quality, raising the question of whether its benefits can be retained without the cost of generating it. We investigate this question with \textbf{GLiDE}, a family of decision models spanning 0.4B to 27B parameters. Building on Qwen hybrid language models, GLiDE enables bidirectional interactions between the context, question, and candidate answers by removing causal masking from full-attention layers. To transfer reasoning capabilities into single-pass inference, we combine soft-target distillation from multiple teachers, including a reasoning model, with progressive post-training on diverse decision tasks. We further explore parameter-free recurrent depth to increase inference-time computation without generating tokens. Across five model sizes, GLiDE lies on the performance--parameter Pareto frontier of the Hugging Face \DI{}, with each model outperforming evaluated alternatives of equal or smaller size. \dmtwo{} (27B) achieves a hidden-set score of 71.52, with an expected calibration error of 2.0\% and a median latency of 92.9\,ms on a single GPU. Further checkpoint averaging and parameter-free recurrent depth yield GLiDE~27B, which reaches 73.37 with an expected calibration error of 2.1\%.

papers.title: Visual Attribution Limits and Graded Provenance Auditing in Commercial Video-Generation APIs
papers.summary: Commercial video-generation APIs bill by model and tier, while intermediaries could substitute cheaper models, lower tiers, or cached clips. What can a delivered file establish about its origin? We combine measurements of passive attribution and cryptographic provenance into a graded audit. We test attribution probes and zero-shot detectors under re-encoding, downscaling, and frame-rate changes, and survey C2PA and GB 45438 metadata across 19 commercial endpoints. Only authenticated provenance supports accusations: tier contradictions or duplicate signed instances under fresh-generation contracts, excluding retries and idempotent returns. Unverifiable signed-endpoint deliveries trigger original-file demands under pass-through clauses; archive-reuse and delivery-parameter screens support review only. Six-model container and bitstream accuracy falls from 83.9% on raw files to 45.3% after uniform re-encoding, using different feature sets. Subsampling real references from 24 to 3 fps raises pooled D3 AUROC from 0.845 to 0.988. Only BytePlus authenticates tier claims under our pinned policy, including 187/187 audited deliveries across three Seedance tiers; tested remuxing and re-encoding leave processed Seedance files unverifiable. The audit identifies authenticated contradictions in 100/100 raw 720p signed tier-swap cases, with zero observed false flags on the tested honest pools.

papers.title: When the Noise Gets Noisy: Quantum Error Correction with Disordered Noise and Misinformed Decoding
papers.summary: Experimental demonstrations of quantum error correction often exhibit noise that varies across space and time, and attempting to characterize this disorder has been shown to substantially improve decoding performance. However, theoretical studies of quantum error correction typically assume fixed, perfectly known, homogeneous noise. Here we model decoding with incomplete or inaccurate knowledge of disordered noise channels by treating physical error rates as random variables. We show that the decoding performance is set by a small number of information-theoretic functionals of the noise distribution: the entropy determines the threshold while Bhattacharyya coefficients bound the deep sub-threshold decay rate of logical failures. Furthermore, our results give a quantitative measure of the benefits of characterizing this noise. We numerically investigate both maximum-likelihood and minimum-weight-error decoding of surface codes, showing good agreement with theory across the code-capacity, phenomenological, and circuit-level noise settings, including with noise distributions seen in open-access superconducting devices. When it comes to error correction in realistic settings, reporting the average entropy and Bhattacharyya coefficient of noise distributions could therefore be more informative than the mean or median error rates of a device's components.

papers.title: Grid Cells as Spectral Successor Features: A Reusable Basis for Continual Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Continual reinforcement learning requires agents to adapt when the task changes while reusing what they know about the environment. Successor features separate dynamics from task-specific reward, but their effectiveness depends on the choice of base features. Taking the identification of entorhinal grid cells with eigenvectors of the successor representation as a design principle, we build this basis from eigenvectors of the transition matrix of a fixed reference policy. With such a basis, the successor features at a state-action pair are a linear combination of the base features at that same pair, which is not true in general, and the coefficients are known in closed form: each successor feature is its base feature multiplied by $θ_i = 1/(1-γλ_i)$, where $λ_i$ is its eigenvalue. The long-term return is thus predicted from the same features as the immediate reward, no successor-feature network or replay buffer is needed, and adapting to a new task reduces to a linear regression on the reward. The agent acts greedily on the action values of the reference policy, which is one step of policy improvement over it and suffices to reach a single goal. In a two-goal gridworld, with the uniform random walk as reference policy, whose eigenvectors are the low-frequency Laplacian eigenvectors, agents built this way maintain near-maximal return across every change of goal, whereas SimpleSF and DQN lose most of their return at each change.
papers.comment: 15 pages, 3 figures. Accepted at the NeurReps and WiML workshops at NeurIPS 2026

papers.title: JARVIS: An Agent That Designs, Builds, and Tests Circuit Boards on Its Own
papers.summary: Power electronics is central to the energy transition, but developing new hardware still relies on human-led design, fabrication, testing, and iteration. We present JARVIS, an embodied AI agent that autonomously closes this loop for circuit boards. JARVIS maintains machine-specific capabilities and constraints, scans its workspace using a robot-mounted 3D scanner, and constructs an executable digital twin in which it rehearses robot motions, fabrication steps, and circuit behavior before consuming materials. A single text instruction initiates the physical experiment. Using unmodified desktop equipment, the agent coordinates a robot arm, a PCB printer that deposits conductive silver ink and solder paste, and a pick-and-place machine. It verifies progress using cameras and sensors, then tests the fabricated circuit with an OPAL-RT real-time simulator and an oscilloscope. Based on the measurements, JARVIS diagnoses deviations from the design and generates a revised design in KiCad for subsequent rehearsal. In a demonstration involving a 60 Hz notch filter for grid-connected converter sensing, JARVIS completed a first-run experiment in 2 h 39 min without human intervention, achieving 50.6 dB attenuation at 60 Hz. Its digital-twin rehearsal identified five issues before fabrication, including a test criterion that would have incorrectly rejected a functioning board. During execution, the agent also resolved encountered faults autonomously. These results demonstrate an integrated agent-driven workflow for physical design, fabrication, measurement, and iterative improvement of power-electronic circuitry. To our knowledge, JARVIS is the first system in power electronics in which an agent closes the physical design-build-test-learn loop for circuit boards.

papers.title: Emergent Orbital Hall Currents in Disordered and Amorphous Materials
papers.summary: The role of disorder in orbital transport remains a central open question in orbitronics. Using a real-space formulation of itinerant orbital angular momentum, we investigate the real-time or- bital Hall transport in single-orbital square-lattice and graphene-based systems. We demonstrate that both structural (polycrystalline and amorphous) and electrostatic disorder can generate siz- able orbital Hall currents that are absent in their pristine counterparts. Remarkably, in amorphous graphene, these currents persist over extended timescales and across a broad energy window around charge neutrality, despite the strong localization of electronic states. Consistent with recent exper- imental evidence, our findings establish amorphous quantum materials as promising platforms for disorder-engineered orbitronic functionality.

papers.title: Lyapunov Theory for Output-to-State Stability of Nonlinear Infinite-Dimensional Systems
papers.summary: For a broad class of nonlinear infinite-dimensional systems with outputs, we show that output-to-state stability (OSS) is equivalent to the existence of a coercive OSS Lyapunov function in implication form. While establishing this equivalence, we prove that OSS is equivalent to uniform global asymptotic stability modulo output, relate these properties to the vanishing output vanishing state property, and highlight new challenges that do not arise in the nonlinear finite-dimensional or linear infinite-dimensional settings. The results are illustrated by a nonlinear reaction-diffusion system with a nonlinear output map.

papers.title: Existence and uniqueness for a coagulation-transport equation
papers.summary: This paper establishes the existence, uniqueness, and regularity of weak solutions to a class of nonlinear coagulation-transport equations describing the asymptotic dynamics of multispecies coalescent processes. The model captures the multi-scale ancestral lineage decay governed by an autonomous drift field, coupled with a time-inhomogeneous quadratic coagulation term parameterized by the initial population mass. By utilizing the metric structure of probability measures, we demonstrate that any weak solution satisfies a unique mild representation formula dictated by the transport semigroup. This characterization allows us to construct a unified narrative where existence, uniqueness, and moment preservation are proved directly through a contractive fixed-point argument in the space of finite Radon measures.

papers.title: The Rate of Convergence of Empirical $(p,q)$-Gromov-Wasserstein Distances
papers.summary: We study empirical convergence rates for $(p,q)$-Gromov-Wasserstein (GW) distances $D_{p,q}$ for arbitrary real exponents $p>0$ and $q\ge1$. Let $μ$ and $ν$ be probability measures on compact metric spaces $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Y}$, and let $\widehatμ_n$ and $\widehatν_m$ be their empirical measures, constructed from independent i.i.d. samples of sizes $n$ and $m$. If the spaces $\mathcal{X},\,\mathcal{Y}$ are compact subsets of the Euclidean spaces $\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ and $\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$, respectively, we obtain an upper bound of order $(n\wedge m)^{-(p\wedge2)/((d_x\wedge d_y)\vee 2(p\wedge2))}$ on the plug-in error of $D_{p,q}^p(\widehatμ_n,\widehatν_m)$ in expectation, up to a logarithmic factor at the critical dimension $d_x\wedge d_y=2(p\wedge2)$. On Euclidean balls, this rate is sharp up to the logarithmic factor. More generally, we show that the same upper bound holds when one space is a compact subset of a complete, connected $d$-dimensional Riemannian manifold and the other has polynomial covering numbers, with $d_x\wedge d_y$ replaced by $d$. Earlier works on $(2,2)$-GW, $(2,1)$-GW and other even-order cases rely on variational representations of GW distances that are specific to their exponents. We instead reduce the plug-in error to an analysis of empirical processes through local duality, which may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Optimal Error corrected Hamiltonian estimation with nuisance parameters
papers.summary: Realistic quantum sensing is often affected by both noise and unknown nuisance parameters. Under Markovian dynamics, existing error correction approaches have often sought to suppress nuisance responses alongside environmental noise. Here we show that this local suppression of nuisance parameters is unnecessary and can be overly restrictive: nuisance parameters and Markovian noise impose fundamentally different constraints and require distinct treatments.
